content.title: Stock Market News From March 31, 2026: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq Rally; Iran War; Worst Quarter Since 2022; Oil Prices Fall; Nvidia Stock, Micron, Tesla, SoFI, More Movers
content.text: Key EventsPinned PostThe stock market marked its best day since May as the first quarter of 2026 wrapped up with renewed hope an end to the Iran war could come sooner rather than later.The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 1,125 points, or 2.5%. The S&P 500 rallied 2.9%. The Nasdaq Composite surged 3.8%. All three marked their best days since May 12, 2025.The yield on the 2-year Treasury note fell to 3.8%. The 10-year yield was down to 4.31%.The market spiked suddenly after reports about Iran’s president. Bloomberg, citing a report from IRNA, wrote that Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian told European Council President António Costa that Iran has "the necessary will to end this war." The report added Iran expects "the essential guarantees to prevent the recurrence of aggression" among other requirements.Though conflicting headlines around U.S.-Iran talks have swirled for weeks, the market was buying first and asking questions later.Artificial intelligence stocks led an early rally this morning after CoreWeave announced an $8.5 billion loan facility to build AI infrastructure. The delayed draw term loan received an investment-grade A3 rating from Moody’s, a first for such loans backed by high-performance computing infrastructure and a customer contract.Mizuho’s Daniel O’Regan tells Barron’s the CoreWeave news sent fellow AI ‘neocloud’ names rallying. Neocloud firms like CoreWeave provide cloud-computing capacity.“Memory is all over the place after mixed feedback on DRAM prices and lingering concerns over TurboQuant,” O’Regan adds. “Semis are rebounding after one of their worst relative performance days in history. Consumer confidence was much better than feared, spurring another leg higher in risk assets.”That doesn’t mean the market is out of the woods. The Nasdaq and Dow are still in correction territory after investors endured violent swings for much of the first quarter of the year.“The headline-driven equity rebound is unfolding in the absence of clear technical evidence that would suggest seller exhaustion and after multiple markets have broken down below key pattern support levels,” writes Jason Hunter, a technical strategist at J.P. Morgan. “We recognize that geopolitical news can lead to a V-shaped bottom. But until the market starts to break above key short-term resistance levels, the technical setup on its own suggests continued vulnerability.”
